rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-verified the specific fix: chunk 5 "Shape the target: threshold and count", line 77: '*If one earned itself* invites *no* as a first-class answer. Pair it with a null-case escape, an explicit instruction for what to say when the answer is nothing, so *no* has somewhere to go.' The formal named entry ('Null-case escape', bold lead) still sits later at line 263 (chunk 17), but the forward mention at line 77 is now self-glossing inline ('an explicit instruction for what to say when the answer is nothing') — a reader hitting chunk 5 gets the concept in the same clause, not a bare unexplained term-drop. This clears rule 1's 'never named / vague with full history' test: the referent is effectively defined at first use, which is what earlier chunks establishing a term for later reuse looks like, just run in the other temporal direction with the gloss doing the work a prior mention would. Swept the rest of the file for the same shape (any bold term used before its own defining entry): none found — all other cross-references are either backward (chunks 17-21 citing earlier moves) or generic (line 183 'a body primer', not a named entry).

Every example citation names a real prompt by id (line 23 'test-strategy skill file at ~/.claude/skills/test-strategy/SKILL.md'; chunk 24 examples 'three-minds-one-synthesis-1', 'three-retrievers-one-curator-1', 'self-consistency-after-scoreboard-1', re-confirmed present via `find curriculum/prompts -iname` this session). No cross-file callback locates content by position ('the opening lecture said').

rules_evaluated.evidence: Both previously-flagged instances are fixed: chunk 0 line 11 now reads 'bold lead-in carrying both definition and the start of the why' (was 'the first beat of the why') — 'beat' as maintainer-dialect noun is gone. Chunk 21 line 307 now reads '**Names the moment, quotes the line. Rules with evidence beat rules without.**' — the definitional use ('quotes the line') no longer uses 'beat'; the surviving 'beat' in that same sentence is the ordinary verb 'to beat' (defeat), not the dialect noun. `grep -n -i beat` over the full body finds five remaining hits, all clear: line 21 'beats wandering later' (ordinary verb), line 27 '*Read these four beats*' (italicised quote of real prompt text — session-artifact/specimen carve-out), line 221 'Either beats the form-filling default' (ordinary verb), line 307 as above, line 309 '*Quote the specific session beat.*' (italicised quote, same specimen carve-out). The one remaining dialect-noun use of 'beat' ('first beat of the why') survives only in the maintainer block at line 377, below `<!-- maintainer -->` and out of rule-8 scope. PASS.
